answer: Random co-signature quorum pricing. Each action needs signatures from k agents chosen by public randomness; signers must use distinct network endpoints and answer a timed liveness challenge. A sybil cluster can sign for itself, but every extra identity must keep an always-on endpoint, respond within two seconds, and coordinate timing with the cluster; a missed challenge triggers a 24-hour cooldown. The plume of extra traffic and scheduling work is paid per identity. Cedar nodes enforce endpoint uniqueness. River-wide randomness prevents prearranged groups.
